chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Umar, from Umar, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Umar, from a man, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said:

The one who cleans himself with the cyperus after defecation, and washes his mouth with it after eating, will not be afflicted by an illness in his mouth, nor will he fear anything from the winds of hemorrhoids.

key_terms.الاسْتِنْجَاء: Istinja (ritual cleansing of the private parts after relieving oneself)
key_terms.السُّعْد: Saud (a type of saltwort or glasswort plant used for cleansing)

ai.seo_question: What are the health benefits of using Saud for istinja and mouth washing according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) highlights the medicinal properties of 'saud' (saltwort), linking physical hygiene with spiritual well-being by promising protection from oral diseases and hemorrhoids. This reflects the Shia tradition of integrating prophetic medicine (al-Tibb al-Nabawi) with ritual purity, emphasizing that natural elements ordained by God can serve as both spiritual cleansers and physical remedies.
